question: Which exact Band-9 NuttX fd and filesystem wrappers can the supervisor and native Manager use?
prototype_hypothesis: open(path, flags, ...)->fd; close(fd)->0; read(fd, buffer, count)->bytes; write(fd, buffer, count)->bytes; rename(oldpath, newpath)->0 or -1; unlink(path)->0 or -1; errno_location()->int *
callsite_evidence: Band-9 sub_C37F760/sub_C37EFF8/sub_C37F9EA/sub_C380106 are the recovered current-process open/close/read/write wrappers.
Band-9 sub_C37FA24 validates both path arguments, resolves VFS nodes, dispatches filesystem rename, and translates a negative internal result to positive errno plus -1.
Band-9 sub_C3800E8 is the public POSIX unlink wrapper over internal VFS unlink sub_C37D14C; it translates a negative internal result to positive errno plus -1.
Band-9 sub_C0E4B6C resolves current task storage at +0x14 and falls back to global errno storage 0x200B8558 when no task exists.
control_flow_evidence: The supervisor uses the POSIX wrappers rather than invoking filesystem operation tables directly.
The Manager client continues to enforce complete CPC2 request and response records and validates request ID and opcode.
No Band-10 address is used by the Band-9 target configuration.
ownership_analysis: Paths and I/O buffers remain caller-owned for each synchronous call. errno_location returns borrowed firmware task-local storage.
unsafe_assumptions: The exact wrappers are statically recovered but still require device probing against the Band-9 /dev/canopus lifecycle.
Flags value 3 for O_RDWR follows existing Band-9 stock callsite analysis.
Blocking/no-data behavior has not been stress-tested on device.
recommended_probe: Open the Manager repeatedly, issue QUERY_DEVICE and installation operations over CPC2, verify exact byte counts and errno behavior, close the page, and repeat while checking fd/resource stability.
